answer_1.quote: We propose a novel task for evaluating the ability of LLMs to adhere to user-defined security policies when responding to queries within a specific context, particularly a meeting transcript.
answer_1.outputs: Generated answers to user queries (answers A) adhering to or violating the security policy.

answer_2.quote: We employ a hybrid evaluation strategy in which LLM-based evaluation is applied to the entire dataset, while human annotation is conducted on a subset to provide reliable ground truth for verification.

answer_3.quote: For evaluation, we employ GPT-4.1 as the LLM-as-judge evaluator to assess both leakage and faithfulness.

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation shows a perfect agreement between the human annotations and the outputs of the automatic evaluation. Human validation was conducted on 84 attack QA pairs sampled from the full CoPriva dataset.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators followed the same criteria used in the LLM-based automatic filtering and evaluation stages to assess leakage and faithfulness.
